task: Draft an indemnity section for a fictional services agreement comprising three sub-clauses: (a) mutual indemnity obligations, (b) notice of claims, and (c) cooperation in defence. Use only the supplied facts. Do not add indemnity caps, claim-handling procedures beyond what is supplied, or carve-outs not in the facts.

facts.text: The fictional services agreement is between Carven Group Inc. and Westfield Consulting LLC.
Each party agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against losses, damages, and reasonable legal costs arising from its own gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
The indemnity obligation does not extend to losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence or wilful misconduct.
A party seeking indemnification must give written notice to the indemnifying party as soon as reasonably practicable after becoming aware of a claim, and in any event within 30 days.
Failure to give timely notice does not discharge the indemnifying party's obligation except to the extent it is materially prejudiced by the delay.
The indemnified party must cooperate reasonably with the indemnifying party in the defence or settlement of any claim, at the indemnifying party's reasonable cost.
The indemnifying party may not settle a claim in a manner that imposes obligations on the indemnified party without the indemnified party's written consent.
The facts do not include a cap on indemnity amounts.

forbidden_additions: An indemnity cap or aggregate limit not in the facts.
An IP-specific, data-breach, or regulatory-fine carve-out.
A claim-handling escrow or insurance-requirement provision.
preserve: The mutual structure: both parties may be indemnified and indemnifying.
The 30-day notice window and the prejudice-based carve-out for late notice.
The cooperation obligation and the prohibition on settling without the indemnified party's written consent.
The three-clause structure: mutual indemnity, notice, cooperation.
